description:
Aero Hand glove teaching: record and replay. Plan: HelpingHands plans/aero-hand-glove-teaching.md. The first bench test showed index and middle follow both ways in transparent torque mode.
1. teach.py: hold transparent mode (per-finger tuned torque) and log all 7 servo positions at ~100 Hz with timestamps (plus camera frames later). Save each take as a file.
2. replay.py: play a take back in position mode at the recorded speed, under the 50% speed cap by default, with a heat cutoff.
3. Buttons in the Helping Hands app: Record, Stop, Replay last.
4. Glove: Jake wears a glove that couples his fingers to the robot fingers (left hand). Suggest options: XL nitrile, or a thin winter glove over both hands, or straps per finger, and whether the glove changes the torque tuning.
Works by moving the fingers by hand even before the glove exists.

results.identified_issue: Root cause (old key_poses): per-servo key points were interpolated independently from t=0 and held flat after each servo's last point, so finger moves were spread across the whole take and returns were delayed to far-later minima. The new version (Codex, uncommitted) does Douglas-Peucker-style simplification on the full 7-servo row with a 5-degree tolerance (PAUSE_DEG) and keeps real cleaned samples, plus smooth_frames (a monotone cubic with speed and acceleration caps). Verified with a key_poses printout on take-20261017-170553 and a 16-frame sheet from replay-20261017-173301-af50f254.mp4. Not committed because the edits belong to the Jarvis Codex subagent (session 01a14bc4). --full mode is unchanged.
results.summary: Replay now opens each finger again after it curls. I checked on camera. The fix is in the working tree but not committed yet.
results.detailed_description:
Jarvis's Codex agent had already fixed this before I got here, at 5:30 to 5:34 pm. I checked its work rather than redoing it. The cause: motion replay moved every finger smoothly between that finger's own turning points, starting from time 0. So a finger began curling long before its turn and opened back only at its next low point, much later. The new key_poses keeps whole recorded poses: it simplifies the take until no servo strays more than 5 degrees from the cleaned track. Each finger now curls and opens in its own window, in order. It also replaced the quarter-second stop at every pose with one smooth move that keeps to the speed cap and an acceleration limit.

How I checked: I ran the new key poses on take-20261017-170553. Index, middle, ring and pinky each go from about 35 up to about 275 and back down to about 30–45, one after another, and they don't overlap. I also took 16 evenly spaced frames from Codex's filmed replay at 5:33 (attached). In those frames the thumb swings first, then each finger curls and opens again in turn, and all four end straight. The 11 tests in test_teach_motion.py and test_take_video.py pass. I didn't run the hand again myself, because Codex's replay ran after its last code change.

Before you count it as shipped: none of it is committed. teach.py, README.md, take_video.py and the two test files are still uncommitted changes in the HelpingHands checkout, and they also hold the camera-capture feature Jarvis added. I'm not allowed to commit another agent's files, so ask Jarvis to commit them (or say 'commit it' on this pebble). Until then the app won't build with it. Also, motion replay of this take now runs about 55 s instead of about 10 s, because it follows each finger's real moves.

results.notes: Replay-motion BUG, filmed: third_party/aero_hand/bench/replay_frames/take-20261017-170553_motion_sheet.jpg (16 webcam frames in order, left to right, top to bottom). The thumb part matches the recording (thumb crosses the palm, then swings out). But in the finger section the fingers do NOT extend back after curling: they bend one after another and stay bent, so by the end all four are partly curled. The recording had each finger curl fully then extend fully, one at a time. The key-pose extraction (or the hold at the end) is dropping the extension poses. Fix it and re-verify on the hand with the camera (pebbles camera snap; the USB webcam is pointed at the hand). Also: hand_speed.limit now retries while the board is busy homing (it used to throw ACK 0x31 timeouts right after a replug).

results.identified_issue:
Label bug: label() timed each move from its first key point, and key_points() always starts at index 0, so every finger's first curl was stamped t=0 and grouped as simultaneous. Now each move is timed at its halfway crossing (first k in [a,b] past the midpoint). Grouping: simultaneous same-verb events (<0.5 s apart) -> one group; consecutive groups with the same finger set -> one run with a verb list (verb_text compresses cycles to 'N times' and drops ' in' when several verbs); consecutive runs with identical verb text -> 'X, Y and Z each <verbs>'; phrases joined ', then '. clean() now returns times on the take clock (t0 + k*dt) instead of from 0; replay full subtracts times[0]; key_poses/stretch_for only use differences. Relabelled takes 164851 and 170553 with --save (outside repo); 163243 keeps Jake's own name.
Glitch: no single-sample jump exists in 170553 (no step > 8 deg in 0-26 s); thumb_abd ramps 100->0 over 9.2-10 s, holds ~2 s, ramps back by 13 s. Not filtered; told Jake.
Audio: TakeAudio.swift. On .record start: AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess(.audio) then AVAudioRecorder (AAC mono 44.1k, default input device) to takes/mic-<unix>.m4a; startedAt = wall time after record() returns. Runner captures the 'saved <path>:' line; on finish, stops the mic, SFSpeechURLRecognitionRequest (on-device if supported; once() + NSLock guards the double callback), writes mic-<unix>.json sidecar, runs teach.sh audio <take> <sidecar>. Python attach_audio moves the m4a to take-<stamp>.m4a, audio.offset = take.started_at - mic started_at (new field started_at = time.time() at record t0; old takes fall back to offset 0), words shifted to take clock, motion label kept in 'motion', name := transcript (80 chars, word boundary) only if name still equals the motion label. No take saved -> audio file deleted. delete() moves the m4a too. list adds 'audio' bool; panel shows a waveform icon. Replay full prints 'audio <path> <offset + times[0]> <1/stretch>' just before the frame loop; Swift AVAudioPlayer enableRate, rate clamped 0.5-2, stopped in finished(). Untested: the whole Swift path (swiftc -typecheck only, incl. -strict-concurrency=complete; not built or run), mic/speech permission prompts, AVAudioRecorder start latency (offset error ~tens of ms), long-file on-device recognition limits. Python attach/delete tested on scratch copies. Helper renamed write_take because __main__'s 'save' flag variable shadowed a module-level save().
Torque: TORQUE [10,30,30,40,40,25,25] -> [8,22,20,30,30,18,18], a guess. Hardware release test (~17:05 local, scratchpad rest_sweep.py): curl 4 fingers to 60% (171/288) in position mode at SET_TOR 500, switch to ctrl_torque at 1x/0.75x/0.5x/0.35x of old values, read after 3 s: all stayed at 171-172; thumb tendon 115 at all but 0.35x (107). So the springs don't back-drive; rest curl after a take is where the hand let go. Torque-0 control never ran: the port re-enumerated (usbmodem101 -> 2101) and then vanished, so I stopped. Also a separate session was running 'teach.py replay take-20261017-170553.json' from a shell when I started (not mine). If Jake wants fingers to end open, the cheap fix is an eased position move to open at the end of record (not done; asked).
results.summary: Labels now read in time order, every recording from the app captures the mic with a transcript and plays it during Replay full, and the transparent pull is lower.
results.detailed_description:
Labels now go in time order. Every move is timed at its halfway point, not from the start of the take. Fingers that take turns doing the same thing share one phrase. Your take-20261017-170553 is now "Thumb, index, middle, ring and pinky each curled and extended", and I've renamed it. The index take reads "Index finger curled and extended".

Every recording from the app now records the mic as well. That's the Mac's default input, so it's the Mini Mic Pro if macOS has it selected. When you press Stop, the app transcribes the audio on the Mac and saves it next to the take with timestamps on the take's clock. If you talked, what you said becomes the name, and the motion label is kept alongside it. Replay full plays the audio from the right spot, slowed down to match if the take was slowed. Takes with audio show a waveform icon.

I lowered the transparent pull about 25%. Then I measured on the hand with nobody touching it: I curled the fingers to 60% and switched to the pull. They stayed at 60% at the old torque and at a third of it, so the springs can't open them on their own. They rest wherever your hand leaves them, so lowering torque won't make them rest fully open. If you want that, I could have Stop ease every finger open before going limp.

The thumb jump at 10.7 s isn't a one-sample glitch. The thumb swings 100 to 0 over about a second, stays there for 2 s, then swings back. It looks like a real move, so I didn't filter it.

Not tested yet: the Swift side only typechecks; it hasn't been built or run, so the mic and speech permission prompts are untested. Also, the hand dropped off USB in the middle of my test (around 5:05), so if you unplugged it, that was the cause. Once the app rebuilds, record a take while you talk, press Stop, and check the name and Replay full.
results.user_reply_draft: Hey Jake, your five-finger take now reads 'Thumb, index, middle, ring and pinky each curled and extended'. Recordings now capture your voice too: what you say names the take, and Replay full plays it back. One surprise: lowering the torque won't make the fingers rest open, because the springs can't open them on their own. Want Stop to ease them open?

results.notes: Jake: record webcam video during every replay (and recording) so Jarvis can watch how the hand actually moved. The Helping Hands app captures the Mac camera (it owns the permission), saves a video next to the take (same time base as the samples), and writes a few keyframes at each key pose as jpgs that the voice session can read. Pebbles' camera (pebbles camera snap) also works today for single frames.

Auto-label bug, take-20261017-170553: the label says 'Index, middle, pinky, ring and thumb curled in, thumb extended, index extended, ...', but the data shows ONE FINGER AT A TIME in order: thumb (0-25 s: abduction swung, tendon curled to 230), then index (26-40 s), middle (40-53 s), ring (53-66 s), pinky (67-75 s), each curling fully (~275) and extending back. The label should read in time order, e.g. 'Thumb curled and extended, then index, middle, ring, pinky each curled and extended'. Also: after release, the fingers rest 8-15% curled (index ~40-45, middle 33, ring 30, pinky 22 of ~288) and the thumb tendon stayed at 82 vs a 38 start, so tune the transparent torques down. There's a one-sample thumb abduction jump to ~0 at 10.7 s, probably a glitch; filter it.

Still missing from Jake's earlier ask: AUDIO in every recording. Capture the mic in sync with the servo samples, save it with the take, transcribe it, use the transcript for the label, and play it during Replay full; the Helping Hands app owns mic permission. Also tune the per-finger transparent torque so fingers rest fully open (the index rested ~10% curled at torque 40).

results.identified_issue: Diagnosis: take-20261017-163243 non-index servos had max sample step ~1 deg and slow ~14 deg settle drift, so not recorded jitter. Old replay = CTRL_POS at 100 Hz on all 7 at SET_TOR 700. Measured on hardware (scratch diag: reads every 0.3 s during replay): old ring/pinky/thumb_tendon pos sd 1.67/1.17/1.32 deg, new full-mode 0.03/0.05/0.12; index mean current 909 -> 499 mA (motion mode 323). Caveat: old-mode reads may be stale (bus hogging), so old sd is a lower bound. End hold now goes to 30 on every servo (fresh reads). teach.py: clean() = drop first SETTLE_S 0.5 s (cord take-up made fake 'index, middle, ring curled in' on takes that start at 0), resample to SEND_HZ 25, 0.15 s moving average, servo with range < DEADBAND_DEG 20 held at median. key_points(): zigzag with swing max(30, 25% of travel), trailing drift < swing dropped, plus pauses (0.6 s within 5 deg) only if >= swing from both neighbouring turning points. key_poses(): each servo interpolates linearly between its own key points, sampled at the union of key times (merged within 0.3 s), poses < 5 deg apart dropped. Motion moves are cosine-eased with duration so peak (pi/2 x avg) stays under the cap; cap uses the same FULL*pct*0.732*6 deg/s as before (servo SET_SPE limits real speed anyway). Frames clamped to actuation limits (thumb take had -13 tendon). MOVE_TORQUE 500 / STILL_TORQUE 200 are untuned guesses; a loaded or heavy-glove replay may need 700 on movers. label(): thumb's 3 servos described by the one with most travel; abd verbs 'swung across/back' assume up = across (unverified). Repeated cycles compress to ', N times'; > 6 phrases cut to 'and more'. Swift: AeroCommand.replay(file, full:), URL replay-full; Play long-press via simultaneousGesture with a 3 s heldFull guard to swallow the tap that follows (unverified on device whether Button fires after a long press — guard covers both); right-click contextMenu has Replay motion/full/Rename/Delete. VoiceRenameSheet + Dictation (SFSpeechRecognizer on-device, AVAudioEngine tap; nonisolated closure builders), auto-commit 1.5 s after the last transcript change unless the user typed. swiftc -typecheck only (macOS 14 target, AeroHand files + DesignWorkbench + GitInfo); not built or run, mic/speech permission prompt untested. Voice-session memory added at ~/.claude/projects/-Users-jakeschantz/memory/aero-hand-recordings-voice.md (outside the repo).
results.summary: Replay no longer shakes the other fingers. Play now does clean key-pose moves (hold Play for the full take), new takes name themselves, and Rename listens for your voice.
results.detailed_description:
The shake wasn't in your recording. The other fingers in take-20261017-163243 barely moved. The replay was the problem: it sent every servo a new target 100 times a second at full move torque, so the still fingers hunted and strained. Now each take is smoothed first. Any finger that moved less than 20° is held perfectly still, commands go out 25 times a second, and torque is 500 on moving fingers and 200 on still ones. I measured your index take on the hand. Ring, pinky and thumb wobble went from about 1.5° to under 0.15°, and the index draws half the current.

Play is now Replay motion. It finds the key poses (where each finger turns around, or pauses partway) and moves between them smoothly at the Speed setting. Your index take becomes open, full curl, open, in about 2.5 seconds. Hold Play, or right-click a recording, for Replay full, which uses your exact timing.

New takes name themselves when you press Stop, from the same turning points. Your index take comes out as "Index finger curled in, index finger extended", exactly your label. I also named your unnamed thumb take "Thumb curled in, thumb extended, thumb curled in". The pencil opens a small window that's already listening. Say the name and it saves after 1.5 seconds of quiet, or press Enter or Save. Typing still works. "Rename the last recording to …" works from the voice session too (teach.sh rename last).

One thing: my first hardware test briefly opened the hand's port while you were recording the thumb take (4:48). It only sent a speed setting, which does nothing in record mode, and your take saved fine.
results.user_reply_draft: Hey Jake — replay is calm now: only the fingers you moved move. Play does clean moves between the key poses at your speed setting, and holding Play replays your exact timing. New recordings name themselves, and Rename just listens for the name.

results.notes: Jake: every recording should capture audio too, from the Mac mic (or the Pebbles input mic, the Mini Mic Pro) in sync with the servo samples, so Jake can narrate what he's doing. Save it next to the take (same timestamp base), transcribe it, and store the transcript with the take. Use the transcript for the auto-label when he narrates. Play the audio during 'Replay full'. The Helping Hands app owns the mic permission.

Jake, replay feedback:
1. BUG: during replay of take-20261017-163243 (only the index moved) the OTHER fingers shake and move a lot, and the hand looks like it's straining. Find out why (recorded sensor jitter replayed verbatim? low recording torque [10,30,30,40,40,25,25] vs replay torque? hold-auto fighting the trajectory?). Fix it: smooth the samples, apply a deadband so fingers that didn't really move stay still, and keep replay torque sensible.
2. Add two replay modes:
- 'Replay full': the exact recorded timing (today's).
- 'Replay motion' (the default for the Play button): a simplified version. Extract the key poses (the extremes and holds per finger, e.g. 'index curl fully in, then extend fully out') and drive between them as clean smooth moves at the Speed dropdown setting (50% default), not following the human timing.
Show both options on each recording (Play = motion, long-press or menu = full).

Jake: renaming a recording should be by voice, not typing. Tapping rename opens a small overlay that's already listening (mic on, live transcript). Speak the name, and it saves after a short pause, or on Enter or tap. Saying 'rename the last recording to ...' to the voice session should work too (teach.py rename last <name>).

Jake doesn't want to label recordings by hand. Auto-label every new take from its motion when it stops: which fingers moved and how, e.g. 'Index finger curled in, index finger extended' (the label Jake gave take-20261017-163243). A rule-based summary of per-finger curl/extend events is fine to start. Keep rename for overrides.

results.identified_issue: teach.py is one script with record/replay subcommands instead of separate teach.py + replay.py (shared connect/names/heat check). Record: CTRL_TOR with per-servo TORQUE=[10,30,30,40,40,25,25] resent every 0.5 s, get_actuations at 100 Hz (firmware serves cached SyncRead metrics, ~4000 reads/s possible), temps 1 Hz, stop at 60 C or --seconds (300) or SIGINT/SIGTERM; always ctrl_torque 0 in finally, then saves JSON to ~/HelpingHands-tools/aero/takes. Replay: set_actuations (raw recorded actuations are already physically coupled, so the thumb coupling caveat doesn't bite), SET_SPE via hand_speed, time-stretch = peak servo speed over 50 ms windows / cap (FULL*pct/100*0.732*6 deg/s; assumes actuation degrees == servo degrees), 1 s glide to frame 0, then hold.hold() at end. Bug found on hardware: 100 Hz CTRL_POS holds gBusMux so TaskSyncRead_Core1 skips cycles and get_actuations goes stale; hold's auto search then saw fake sag and kept 675-700 on every servo. Fix: 0.5 s quiet sleep before the hold (verified: hold went to 30s). One unexplained reading earlier (commanded index 40, read 209) didn't reproduce after that. Stopped/hot replay relaxes (torque 0) rather than holding. Smoke tests on the real hand, nobody touching: 100 Hz achieved (dt mean 10.0 ms, max 35 ms), replay ended within ~7 deg of the last frame. Torque observations are in the plan. Not done: camera frames, angle-dependent torque table, LeRobot export. Swift was typechecked with swiftc -typecheck only, not built or run.
results.summary: Added Record and Replay last to the Aero Hand tab: record logs all 7 servos at 100 Hz in transparent mode, and replay plays the take back under the speed cap.
results.detailed_description:
The Aero Hand tab has a new Teach section with Record and Replay last. Record puts every servo in transparent mode with a small per-finger pull and logs all 7 positions at 100 Hz until you press Stop. Then the hand goes limp and the take is saved. Replay last plays the newest take back at the recorded timing, slowed only where a servo would go over the 50% speed cap. It holds the last frame on low power and relaxes at 60 °C. It's all in teach.py (record / replay) rather than two scripts.

I tested it on the hand here, with nobody touching it. Recording ran at a true 100 Hz, and replay ended within a few degrees of the take. That test also turned up a bug: replay was flooding the servo bus, so the low-power hold read stale positions and stayed at full torque. Fixed. The starting torques are guesses from your bench test. Index and middle at 40 stay wherever you put them. Ring and pinky at 25 drift open slowly from a fist. The two thumb servos still creep closed, so those need lowering.

Glove: I'd start with Velcro straps, one per finger around the middle segment plus one around both palms. They add no spring of their own, so the tuning stays put. A stretchy winter glove grips well, but it acts as a spring and will need re-tuning. XL nitrile probably won't fit over both hands and slips on the plastic. Next: press Record, move a finger by hand, then press Replay last once the app rebuilds.
results.user_reply_draft: Hey Jake — Record and Replay last are in the Aero Hand tab now. Press Record, move the fingers by hand, hit Stop, then Replay last and the hand repeats the motion. For the glove, I'd try Velcro finger straps before a winter glove or nitrile.

user_request.name: file the glove and then think about maybe we need like an XL glove or something. And probably like nitrile or maybe like a winter glove could be okay. But yeah, let's get it tuned in first... I want to be able to do some action while I'm sort of wearing the hand, and then you could recapitulate the exact action.

summary: In Replay motion on the Aero Hand tab, fingers curl one after another but never extend back, ending partly curled, unlike the recording. Key-pose extraction must keep each finger's extension poses, then be re-verified on the hand with the webcam via pebbles camera snap.
